name: Andalakkum Aiyan Temple, Thiruaadhanur
deity: Vishnu as Andalakkum Aiyan, reclining with a measuring vessel, with the Goddess Bhargavi (Ranganayaki)
period: A Divya Desam of the Chola country between the Kaveri and the Kollidam, sung by Thirumangai Alvar in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham
summary: At Thiruaadhanur near Swamimalai, Vishnu reclines as Andalakkum Aiyan, the lord with the measuring vessel who, tradition holds, paid Thirumangai Alvar's temple-builders — a Chola Nadu Divya Desam.

sections.history: Thiruaadhanur is a village near Swamimalai, close to Kumbakonam, set in the rich country between the Kaveri and the Kollidam. Its temple is one of the 108 Divya Desams, the abodes of Vishnu sung by the Alvars in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham, and belongs to Chola Nadu. The Lord here is Andalakkum Aiyan — 'the master who measures and rules' — with the Goddess Bhargavi, also called Ranganayaki. The shrine is bound up with Thirumangai Alvar, who sang it and whose great labour of renovating the Srirangam temple is remembered in the legend of this place. The village name itself is traced to Kamadhenu, the wish-granting cow: Thiru-aa-than-oor, 'the sacred place of the cow'.
sections.architecture: The temple follows the Dravidian plan of the Kaveri delta, its sanctum crowned by the Pranava Vimana, named for the sacred syllable Om. Within, the Lord reclines facing east and is shown with a marakkal, the measuring vessel of the paddy country, which devotees read as a sign that he weighs the hearts of those who come to him. Kamadhenu and her calf Nandini are present in the sanctum, recalling the cow's penance, and the temple tank is the Surya Pushkarini.
sections.legends: Tradition holds that Kamadhenu performed penance here and was blessed with the Lord's darshan. The best-loved story, however, belongs to Thirumangai Alvar. Renovating the Srirangam temple, he ran short of money to pay his workers, and on the bank of the Kollidam he met a merchant who had no coins — only a marakkal. The merchant measured out sand to the labourers, promising it would turn to gold for those who had truly worked; for the idle it stayed sand. Devotees believe the merchant was the Lord himself, and so he is Andalakkum Aiyan.
sections.festivals: A ten-day Brahmotsavam is celebrated around May–June, and Vaikunta Ekadashi in Margazhi (December–January) is observed as at every Sri Vaishnava shrine. Between festivals the temple is quiet, and the legend of the measured sand is the story pilgrims carry home. Confirm festival dates with the temple each year.
sections.experience: Look closely at the sanctum: the reclining Lord with his measuring vessel, and Kamadhenu with her calf beside him, make this one of the most distinctive images among the Kaveri Divya Desams. It is a modest village temple, unhurried outside festival days. Thiruaadhanur pairs naturally with Thirupullabhoothangudi and with the Murugan temple of Swamimalai, all within a short drive of Kumbakonam.

visit.timings: Open daily for morning and evening darshan, with a midday closure; festival days are the busiest. Confirm current timings locally before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear is removed before entering. Follow posted rules and the guidance of the priests.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow posted rules and the guidance of the priests.
visit.gettingThere: Thiruaadhanur (Adhanur) is a village near Swamimalai in Thanjavur district, a short drive from Kumbakonam by road. Kumbakonam has the nearest railway station; Tiruchirappalli has the nearest airport.
